context:
Lift the filter in `_query_timings` only. Leave the `run_type == "measurement"` selection inside `_query_display_ms` and `_geomean_ms`, so every derived figure keeps its current definition and the corpus snapshot is provably unchanged except for added `query_executions` rows.

Add a per-result basis-availability summary to the read model so the UI can disable a basis a bundle never recorded (legacy bundles ingested before this change, runs configured with zero warmup, queries that lost a pass) instead of rendering a silently empty comparison.

Prove the no-change property by diffing every non-`query_executions` table between a pre-change and post-change snapshot built from the same corpus at the same SHA. Gate explicitly on the RG-2 range-read byte budget, because `query_executions` grows by roughly a third and that table is range-read in the browser.
description:
The explorer pipeline discards every non-measurement query row at ingest. `_query_timings` in `_project/scripts/explorer_pipeline/transformer.py` skips any row whose `run_type` is not `measurement`, so the published browser snapshot contains no warmup executions at all.

Verified counts over the 213 bundles in `results-explorer/public/data/bundles/` (scanned 2026-08-29): run_type is `measurement` 25,532 rows, `warmup` 8,338 rows, `metadata` 60 rows, `summary` 6 rows.

NOTE THE FOUR VALUES. run_type is NOT a two-valued field. The `metadata` and `summary` rows are not executions at all -- the observed metadata rows carry ms=0 and status=SKIPPED with synthetic ids such as QAPPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT_GROUPBY -- and lifting the ingest filter naively would ingest all 66 of them into query_executions as if they were timed runs. The filter must be narrowed to admit warmup, not removed.

The raw data is otherwise already shaped correctly. Bundles record one object per execution -- {"id", "iter", "ms", "rows", "run_type", "status", "stream", "test_type"} -- with iter 0 for warmup and 1..N for measurement. The snapshot table `query_executions` already declares run_type, iter and stream columns (`_project/scripts/explorer_pipeline/duckdb_builder.py`). Only the ingest filter stands between the corpus and a warmup-aware UI.

Every measurement-basis surface in the approved design -- warmup vs warm median, warm pass 1 vs warm pass 3, min vs median, and the per-pass view on Result Detail -- is unbuildable until those rows reach the snapshot. This item admits warmup rows and makes pass provenance an explicit part of the read model WITHOUT changing a single published figure.

The published-figure invariant is the whole risk. `display_ms` is defined by `_query_display_ms` as the median of passing measurement rows, and display_geomean_ms, geomean_ms, power_score, ranking eligibility, comparison eligibility and every leaderboard position derive from it. Widening what `_query_timings` returns must not widen what those functions consume.

anti_patterns.dont: Accept a snapshot-size regression on the grounds that the data is useful.
anti_patterns.instead: Measure against the RG-2 budget at w0 and take the aggregate-only fallback if the raw rows do not fit.
anti_patterns.why: The byte budget is a shipped capability gate; blowing it degrades cold-load time for every visitor, including those who never open a comparison.

anti_patterns.dont: Add a second per-pass table alongside query_executions.
anti_patterns.instead: Populate the existing query_executions table, which already declares run_type, iter and stream.
anti_patterns.why: A parallel table would drift from the one the browser already range-reads and would double the snapshot growth this item is trying to bound.

anti_patterns.dont: Delete the run_type check in _query_timings outright so every row is ingested.
anti_patterns.instead: Narrow the filter to an explicit allow-list of measurement and warmup.
anti_patterns.why: The corpus contains metadata and summary pseudo-rows with ms=0 and SKIPPED status; ingesting them would put 66 fake zero-millisecond executions into query_executions and into any min statistic computed from it.

anti_patterns.dont: Infer a missing warmup pass as 'warmup equals the first measurement pass'.
anti_patterns.instead: Record basis availability honestly and let the UI disable the basis with a stated reason.
anti_patterns.why: A fabricated warmup value would make the warmup-penalty figure a lie, and that figure is the stated justification for excluding warmup from rankings.

anti_patterns.dont: Remove the run_type filter from _query_display_ms or _geomean_ms as well, so warmup rows start feeding published figures.
anti_patterns.instead: Widen only _query_timings; the display and geomean helpers keep selecting measurement rows internally.
anti_patterns.why: Warmup is a cold-cache pass. Letting it into display_ms would silently move every leaderboard position and invalidate every published comparison.

preserves.behavior: Bundles that never recorded a warmup pass must remain fully valid and ingestible; absence of warmup is not an error.
Leaderboard ordering and meta_leaderboard ranks must be unchanged for the committed corpus.
The RG-2 range-read byte budget must still pass after the snapshot grows.
display_geomean_ms, geomean_ms, sample_geomean_ms, power_score and percentile_stats must be bit-identical for every existing corpus bundle before and after this change.
display_ms must remain the median of passing measurement-run executions per logical query. Widening _query_timings must not widen what _query_display_ms consumes.
is_valid_display_timing, timing_exclusion_reason, display_exclusion_reason, comparison_exclusion_reason and ranking_exclusion_reason must not change for any existing bundle.
run_type rows other than measurement and warmup must never reach query_executions. metadata and summary rows are not executions; the observed metadata rows carry ms=0 and status=SKIPPED.
sample_count must continue to count only the executions that fed display_ms, not the newly ingested warmup rows.

prior_art.concept: `query_executions` already declares run_type/iter/stream and is populated by `_populate_query_executions`. No new table is needed for per-pass data.
`_query_timings` is the single ingest filter that drops warmup rows; `_query_display_ms` and `_geomean_ms` independently re-filter to measurement rows. Widen the first, leave the other two alone.
Existing release-blocking snapshot invariant checker. Add basis-availability and warmup-presence invariants here rather than creating a second checker.
Declared browser snapshot contract; must be updated in the same change as any column or semantic addition.
RG-2 byte budget (10% of on-disk DB per cold load) is the existing gate on snapshot growth. Reuse it as this item's growth gate.

Open medium-high gate that must independently certify real-corpus geomean, percentile and ranking direction. The no-change invariant proven in w3 is exactly the property that gate certifies; hand it the table-level diff as evidence rather than re-deriving it.

Open planning item to rewrite explorer transformer.py to typed models throughout. This item edits the same file for a narrow behavioural reason and deliberately does NOT attempt that rewrite; the rewrite item stays open and is not superseded. Keep this change small enough to rebase onto it.

work_units.evidence: Modified _query_timings in transformer.py to admit measurement and warmup while filtering out metadata/summary non-execution pseudo-rows; updated _query_display_ms to only use measurement rows (fallback to unlabelled legacy, never warmup); verified geomean_ms and sample_count isolation. work_units.notes:
In `_query_timings`, stop skipping rows whose run_type is not `measurement`. Keep every other field mapping identical, including the id/query_id fallback, the ms/execution_time_ms fallback and the pass-status normalisation.

Confirm by reading the code -- not by assuming -- that `_query_display_ms` and `_geomean_ms` each still select `run_type == "measurement"` from whatever list they are handed, and that their fallback-to-all-passing-rows branch cannot now pick up warmup rows for a bundle that has measurement rows. That fallback is the sharp edge: before this change a bundle with no measurement rows fell back to an empty list; after it, the same bundle would fall back to warmup rows. Decide deliberately and write the decision in the code as a comment.

DECISION GATE: if the fallback branch would change behaviour for any bundle in the committed corpus, fix the fallback to be explicit about measurement-only before proceeding to w2.
